title: Raschke Holy Grail on 15m: ADX above 30, first pullback to the 20 EMA, buy the break of the prior bar high

source.title: Holy Grail Setup (Raschke and Connors, Street Smarts 1995, restated)

rule_summary: 15m closed bars; signal at a bar close, fill at the next open. Indicators on 15m: ADX(14), +DI(14), -DI(14) with Wilder smoothing; EMA20 of close. TOUCH bar s: ADX(s-1) > 30 AND ADX(s-1) > ADX(s-5) (strong and rising) AND +DI(s-1) > -DI(s-1) AND EMA20(s) > EMA20(s-4) AND close(s-1) > EMA20(s-1) AND low(s) <= EMA20(s) (first tag from above). ENTRY: in the 3 bars after s, the first bar t with close(t) > high(t-1) AND close(t) > EMA20(t), if flat and fewer than 3 entries today (UTC) on this pair; buy at the open of t+1. A setup is used once. STOP = min(lowest low of bars s..t, entry*0.99), so at least 1% below entry; skip the trade if the lowest low of s..t is more than 2.5% below close(t). TAKE-PROFIT = entry + 1.5*(entry - stop). TIME EXIT at the close of the 32nd bar after entry (8 hours). No higher-timeframe filter.
mechanism: ADX above 30 and rising marks a strong directional run in which directional (often informed or forced) buyers keep arriving. The first dip to the 20 EMA comes from short-term profit takers and mean-reversion sellers paying for immediacy; trend-followers who missed the move and limit buyers absorb it, and the stop-entry above the prior bar's high waits until the selling has paused. The source states no published win rate; the mechanism is momentum continuation after a liquidity-driven pullback. It differs from the lab's EMA snapback and dip rules, which buy stretches below the mean; this buys only the first tag inside an ADX-confirmed 15m trend. A stop of at least 1% keeps the 0.30% round trip under 0.3R, and the 1.5R target is a gross move of at least 1.5%.
